newsitem.title: USA: Split FTC staff recommends Staples merger.
newsitem.headline: Split FTC staff recommends Staples merger.

text.p: A split Federal Trade Commission staff has recommended the commissioners approve the merger of office supply superstores Office Depot Inc. and Staples Inc., a source familiar with the staff's views said Wednesday.
The staff sent a draft "consent decree" to the commissioners which would permit the restructured $4 billion deal to go through, the source said. Some staff members did not like the proposed decree.
"It was a split recommendation," said a person familiar with the staff's views.
An FTC spokeswoman had no comment, nor did a spokesman for Staples.

The five-member commission voted 4-1 last month to challenge the proposed merger in U.S. District Court. Afterwards, commissioners said they would look at any serious new proposals by Office Depot and Staples.

A few days later, Office Depot and Staples announced an agreement in principle to divest 63 stores in 17 markets to the other player in the field, OfficeMax Inc.. All sides said the price was a bargain for OfficeMax at $108.75 million.
In recent days, the five commissioners received a draft of a proposed consent decree from FTC staff, setting out new conditions for the merger.
On Monday, the commissioners set a meeting for Friday at 10 a.m., although the subject of the meeting was not announced.
Together, Office Depot and Staples operate more than 1,000 office superstores in the United States.
The commissioners and staff have mostly been quiet on the deal, but a few have made public comments.

William Baer, director of the FTC bureau of competition, said in a speech at Georgetown Law School last month that the commission had turned down the original deal because it was "fundamentally flawed."
But FTC Chairman Robert Pitofsky said later the deal was potentially "fixable."

The debate over the proposed merger has been very public. For example, the FTC opened up its Web site to e-mail on the merger and got more than 300 comments a day during the first five days it was active.
